name: Limit NERC registration to new loads

letters.desc: The filer argues large load entities that own BES facilities should be registered as Transmission Owners and Transmission Operators under NERC rules, ensuring they fall under mandatory reliability compliance obligations.
quotes: Authorize NERC to register large load entities as Transmission Owners and Transmission Operators if the new large load interconnecting facilities qualify as BES Elements and are not turned over to the incumbent connecting Transmission Owners and Transmission Operators for operation and maintenance after commissioning.

letters.desc: ODEC supports registering large loads with NERC and enhancing existing reliability standards to address the additional operational complexities that large-load campuses, including those with multiple distribution substations, introduce to the grid.
quotes: ODEC supports requiring utilities serving large loads to meet all applicable NERC reliability standards and OATT provisions.

letters.desc: PJM recommends DOE use its authority under Section 403(a) of the DOE Organization Act to direct FERC to order NERC to develop large load registration requirements and reliability standards, and supports the NERC Large Load Task Force as the primary forum for setting those standards.
quotes: The NERC Large Load Task Force is well-equipped to continue its work in exploring cutting-edge issues relating to the planning for and operational complexities of a grid with growing large load saturation.  That industry wide forum drawing together deep subject matter expertise is the best forum to develop new standards and issue other necessary guidance to inform reliable system operations and planning involving large loads.

letters.desc: ELCON opposes mandatory NERC registration for traditional industrial loads, accepting only limited registration for data centers with targeted, minimal burdens. Any new registration must not inadvertently reclassify industrial owners as public utilities under FPA Section 201(e).
quotes: ELCON maintains that the electric system has reliably served industrial load for decades and it remains unnecessary to require owners/operators of traditional large industrial loads to be NERC registered entities and subjected to mandatory reliability standards.

ELCON does not oppose limited registration for data centers and other computational loads as described by NERC's Large Load Task Force in Whitepaper #1 that carry minimal compliance burdens that are commensurate with specifically identified reliability risks posed by the nature of these emerging loads.

ELCON respectfully urges FERC to ensure that these changes do not have the unintended consequence of making new registrants "public utilities" under the broad definition of that term in Section 201(e) of the FPA.

letters.desc: MISO flags that loads, unlike generators, are not currently required to register with NERC, making the option-to-build provision and other obligations drawn from generator rules impractical to extend to load customers without first resolving the registration gap.
quotes: bulk power system owners, operators, and users must register with NERC to ensure compliance with mandatory reliability standards.  This includes generators.  However, loads are not currently required to register with NERC.  Therefore, there would currently be no responsibility or accountability for loads that build interconnection facilities or network upgrades.  Consequently, MISO views this principle as impractical.
